a1.label: 1. Advantage of conventional programming?
a1.why: The text says every line is written and understood by a human in conventional programming.

a2.label: 2. AI assistants make routine tasks...
a2.why: The text says developers complete routine tasks up to 40 per cent faster with AI tools.

a3.label: 3. AI assistants draw suggestions from...
a3.why: The text says AI assistants draw on millions of open-source examples.

a4.label: 4. One risk of AI-suggested code?
a4.why: The text says suggested code may contain bugs the developer does not notice.

a5.label: 5. Why does the IP question exist?
a5.why: The text says suggestions can resemble existing licensed code.

a6.label: 6. The recommendation is to...
a6.why: The text recommends adopting Copilot internally but keeping strict review for customer-facing code.

b1.label: 1. Finding and fixing errors in code
b1.why: ‘Debugging’ means finding and fixing errors in code.

b2.label: 2. Colleagues check your code before merging
b2.why: A ‘code review’ is when colleagues check your code before it is merged.

b3.label: 3. A step-by-step procedure
b3.why: An ‘algorithm’ is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.

b4.label: 4. Can be read, modified, shared by anyone
b4.why: ‘Open-source’ software can be read, modified and shared by anyone.

b5.label: 5. Copyright and patents protect...
b5.why: Copyright and patents protect intellectual property.

b6.label: 6. Unbalanced training data causes...
b6.why: Unbalanced training data can cause a model to show bias.

b7.label: 7. Describes all phases of development
b7.why: The ‘SDLC’ (Software Development Life Cycle) describes all phases from planning to maintenance.

c1.label: 1. Copilot is a tool ___ suggests code
c1.why: ‘That’ introduces a defining relative clause about a thing (a tool).

c2.label: 2. Slower; ___, it gives full control
c2.why: ‘X; however, Y’ is the standard pattern for a contrast after a semicolon.

c3.label: 3. ___ AI tools are fast, suggestions must be checked
c3.why: ‘Although X, Y’ is the standard pattern for a concession at the start of a sentence.

c4.label: 4. A developer ___ uses AI tools...
c4.why: ‘Who’ introduces a defining relative clause about a person.

c5.label: 5. Copilot uses open-source code, ___ conventional programming...
c5.why: ‘X, whereas Y’ is the standard pattern for a direct contrast between two clauses.

c6.label: 6. Bias is a problem ___ can cause unfair results
c6.why: ‘That’ introduces a defining relative clause about a thing (a problem).

c7.label: 7. The code ___ the AI suggested...
c7.why: ‘Which’ introduces a defining relative clause about a thing (the code).
